content:
We have carbon NMR shifts list. Need number of methyl groups (CH3). Methyl carbons typically appear around 10-30 ppm for aliphatic methyls. In list we have peaks: 14.05, 18.60, 22.65, 27.60, 28.70, 31.31, plus higher ones (67-89). Likely methyls are low-field peaks: 14.05, 18.60, 22.65, 27.60, 28.70, 31.31 maybe some are methylene or quaternary. Need to determine number of CH3 groups. Could also use HSQC to see which carbons have attached protons. But we can infer: typical methyl carbon ~10-30 ppm. There are 6 peaks in that region. However some could be methylene (CH2) also around 20-40 ppm. Need more info. Could retrieve HSQC to see which carbons have attached protons and multiplicity? HSQC shows correlation of each carbon with attached protons. But we need count of methyl groups, not just carbon count. Could also get proton NMR to see number of methyl signals (singlets, doublets, etc). Simpler: use HSQC to identify which low-field carbons have 3 attached protons (i.e., methyl). However HSQC only shows correlation, not multiplicity. Could use DEPT, but not available.

Maybe we can retrieve proton NMR and count methyl signals. Let's get proton NMR.
